notes: A song you paused and then left alone could only be started again by opening the app: ten minutes into the background the phone player took SideCut off the lock screen, out of the shade player and out of the now bar.
Pausing now keeps that entry and its buttons in place - previous, play-pause and next - and simply tells the phone the truth: the song is paused, so there is always something to press play on.

Android draws all of those from the media session: the lock screen, the shade player, the quick-settings media player (Samsung shows the same thing in its Now Bar) and the home-screen widget all start the song again where you left it, with SideCut closed.

Nothing extra is left running to hold the entry there. The refresh timer and the wake lock are handed back the moment the player parks, exactly as they were when the session used to be dropped, so a paused SideCut still lets the phone sleep.

A press from outside repairs the deck too: if the page came back with nothing loaded on it - a reload, or audio the phone reclaimed - the press puts your last song back on and starts it instead of doing nothing.
The phone player is on by default, and it is a real setting now in Settings - More - Notification player - the same switch the empty library screen offers, which used to be the only place it existed.
